sentences.text:
These appeals arise out of the common judgment and award dated 04.07.2019 passed in M.V.C.
Nos.2507/2017 and 2508/2017 by the XI Additional District and Additional MACT, Belagavi (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal').
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3580 HC-KAR 2.
The brief facts leading rise to filing of this appeal are as follows:
Shri .
Sanjay S/O Krishan Navakhandkar vs Shri.Mohammed S/O G.D. Ali Saheb Ansar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139191447/
3 On 03.10.2017, at about 12:05 a.m., a road traffic accident occurred.

In the said accident, the RCC roof building belonging to the claimant in M.V.C. No.2508/2017,
situated on the service road of NH-4 (PB Road) at Honaga, Belagavi, was damaged.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the truck bearing registration No.KA-20/C-4957 by its driver, which was proceeding from Mangaluru to Mumbai.

The said vehicle was owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2.
3.

The claimant in M.V.C. No.2508/2017 got the building repaired by spending a huge amount and therefore filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act seeking compensation for the damage caused to the building.
4. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2507/2017 was running a tyre puncture shop situated on the side of the service road of NH-4.
Due to the said accident, the shop and the instruments kept therein were damaged.
It is contended that the petitioner had invested about 5,00,000/- in the said business and was NC: 2026:KHC-D:3580 HC-KAR earning about 30,000/- per month.
Due to the damage caused to the shop, he could not carry out avocation for about 3 to 4 months.
Hence, he filed this claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act seeking compensation for the damage caused to his shop.
5. Notice was issued to the owner of the vehicle.
Despite service of notice, the respondent-owner of the vehicle remained unrepresented and he was placed ex-parte by the Tribunal.

6. The Insurance Company filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and also contended that the driver of the truck was not possessing a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and no fitness certificate or permit was produced.

Hence,
prays to dismiss the claim petition as against respondent No.2.
7.
Both the claim petitions were clubbed together by the Tribunal and common issues were framed.
8. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2507/2017 was examined as PW-1 and also examined another witness as PW-4.
The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2508/2017 examined himself NC: 2026:KHC-D:3580 HC-KAR as PW-2 and examined another witness as PW-3.
The petitioners in both the cases got the documents marked in common as Exs.P1 to P19.

On behalf of the Insurance Company, its Deputy Manager was examined as RW-1 and three documents were marked as Exs.R1 to R3.
9.

The Tribunal, after assessing the oral and documentary evidence on record, allowed the claim petitions in part with costs and awarded a compensation of 60,000/- in MVC No.2507/2017 and 80,000/- in MVC No.2508/2017.
The Tribunal fastened the liability on the owner of the truck.

However, since the said truck was insured with respondent No.2, the Tribunal directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Shri.Sanjay S/O Krishan Navakhandkar vs Shri.

Mohammed S/O G.D. Ali Saheb Ansar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139191447/
4 10.
The petitioners, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, have filed these appeals seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.
11. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

12. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have produced records to show that they sustained NC: 2026:KHC-D:3580 HC-KAR damage to the building as well as to the shop of the petitioner in MVC No.2507/2017.
He further submits that the petitioner also suffered loss in business for a period of 3 to 4 months.
Hence, he contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
On these grounds, he prays to allow the appeals.
13. Notice was issued to the respondent No.1.
Despite service of notice, respondent No.1 remained unrepresented before this Court.
14. Respondent No.2 submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to dismiss the appeals.

15. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
16.
It is an undisputed fact that the petitioner in MVC No.2508/2017 is the owner of the building and the petitioner in MVC No.2507/2017 owns a puncture shop.
Both the building and the shop were damaged due to the accident.
The accident occurred on account of the rash and negligent driving of the truck by its driver.

The petitioner has produced the charge sheet, marked as Ex.P5,
which clearly discloses that the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3580 HC-KAR accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
17.
Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioners in both cases examined witnesses to prove the damage caused to the building and the shop.

PW-3 produced an estimation report, marked as Ex.P-12, and the building plan, marked as Ex.P-13, which clearly demonstrates that the petitioner in MVC No.2508/2017 has incurred expenditure to repair the building.
18. Considering the evidence of PW-3 and PW-4, the Tribunal assessed the damages at 60,000 in MVC No.2507/2017 and 80,000 in MVC No.2508/2017.
On perusal of the evidence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

19. This Court is of the opinion that the petitioner in MVC No.2507/2017 is entitled to global compensation of 1,10,000/- including the amount already awarded by the Tribunal, and the petitioner in MVC No.2508/2017 is entitled to global compensation of 1,30,000/- including the amount already awarded.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3580 HC-KAR 20.

Hence, in view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following order:

sentences.text: ORDER (i) The appeals are allowed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award  passed in MVC Nos.2507/2017 and 2508/2017 by the Tribunal are hereby modified.

(iii) The petitioner in MVC No.2507/2017 is entitled to global compensation of 1,10,000/- including the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, and the petitioner in MVC No.2508/2017 is entitled to global compensation of 1,30,000/- including the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
(iv) The rest of the judgment passed by the Tribunal is hereby maintained.

(v) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3580 HC-KAR certified copy of this judgment, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation of the amount.
(vi) The appellants/claimants are not entitled to interest for the delayed period in filing the appeals in both the cases.
(vii) The Tribunal records, and the amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned, forthwith.

Sd/-
(ASHOK S. KINAGI) JUDGE RHR/-CT: UMD List No.: 1 Sl No.: 20 Shri.
